[Browse the releases](releases.qmd){.btn .btn-primary .me-2 .mb-2}
[Try it in your browser](explorer/index.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary .me-2 .mb-2}
[View on GitHub](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-on-ice){.btn .btn-link .mb-2}

Bioconductor distributes annotation as software: one versioned R package per
organism per release. bioc-on-ice publishes the same knowledge as open tables
that R, Python, DuckDB, a browser or an AI assistant can query directly. That
covers gene annotation for every species at once (NCBI Gene across 51,796 taxa,
Ensembl across 276 species), identifier mappings, GO and other ontologies,
orthologs, interactions, pathways, GWAS associations and literature links.
Each row names the source that asserts it, so providers sit side by side
instead of being reconciled into one view.

```sql
-- DuckDB (CLI, R or Python): no download, no credentials
ATTACH 'https://data.bioconice.cancerdatasci.org/latest/bioconice.duckdb' AS bioc (READ_ONLY);
SHOW ALL TABLES;
```

::: {.grid .mt-4}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .card .p-3}
#### Get the data {.mt-0}

Every table is a plain Parquet file plus a view in `bioconice.duckdb`, served
over HTTPS with range requests. [Releases](releases.qmd) lists every version,
its tables, sizes and row counts.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .card .p-3}
#### Cite a release {.mt-0}

Weekly releases are for querying in place. Monthly releases on Hugging Face
are the permanent copy to cite. See [Versions and
citation](guides/versions-and-citation.qmd).
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .card .p-3}
#### Try it in your browser {.mt-0}

The [Explorer](explorer/index.qmd) browses tables and column docs and runs SQL
against `latest/` with DuckDB-Wasm, and every SQL example on this site opens in
the DuckDB Shell.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .card .p-3}
#### Ask an assistant {.mt-0}

The [MCP server](guides/mcp.qmd)
gives an AI assistant the same read-only access. It runs on your machine:
`uvx --from git+https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-on-ice bioconice-mcp`.
:::

:::

Large data stays where it lives: the `resource` tables catalog datasets in
CELLxGENE, ENCODE, BEDbase and the eQTL Catalogue and point at the original
files. Per-source guides: [BugSigDB](sources/bugsigdb.qmd).
